davincifire.headline: The smallest audience of the five, and some of the biggest Reels. Staff on camera showing something new is what travels.
points: Visual style
Raw phone footage from the showroom, the factory, the training centre and the office. Almost nothing staged or rendered (2 of 24 posts). Bold white subtitles and title cards on most Reels.
Topics and series

Staff product demos (custom sizes, see-through, corner and pier units), the GreenSmart holographic electric launch, the Travis Fire App, and group content shared with the sister brands of Travis Industries: the President's Club dealer event, factory and training, Made in America, office culture.
Video style
19 of 24 posts are Reels. Own Reels run 20 to 62 seconds with a person talking to camera, subtitles and music underneath. Group Reels run up to 89 seconds.
How they write
Short, conversational captions with product specifics. Hashtags dropped to zero from 9 September. Calls to action are occasional: the website, a phone number, "What will you design?".
Who appears
Staff and sales reps in most product Reels, factory workers, dealers at the President's Club. No creators and no paid partners.
Community
No replies to comments in the five posts checked, including one with 15 comments.
davincifire.read: DaVinci talks to dealers and the trade, and more than half its grid (13 of 24 posts) is group content from its sister brands. Its reach comes from its own product novelty demos: the holographic reveal reached 65,759 views, the modular options 49,256 and the holographic 50 inch demo 38,990, on an account with 3,130 followers. Group and culture Reels sit between 1,337 and 8,318. The lesson is not the format, it is the subject: a person showing something people have not seen before.
borrow: A staff member on camera demoing a genuinely new feature. Their three holographic and modular Reels are the reason this small account beats bigger ones.
Subtitles on every Reel with a person speaking.
An explainer on a worry people already have (their Washington gas legislation Reel drew 15 comments, the most of their period).
gaps: No homeowner content: no real homes, no designers, no creators.
More than half the grid is the parent group talking about itself.

modernflamesusa.headline: The brand barely posts. Its grid is other people's work, and that work brings all of its reach.
points: Visual style
Real installed projects: dealer and designer photos of finished rooms, outdoor lanais, creator renovations shot on a phone. The four own posts are clean rendered rooms or flame close ups.
Topics and series

Dealer and designer project reposts as shared posts, creator renovation Reels, and the odd product launch on its own account (Orion V2 in May, the 250th Celebration Flame in July). The Landscape Pro Multi is pushed through dealers since late October.
Video style
6 Reels in six months, only one of them its own (8 seconds, a flame loop, kept off the grid). Creator Reels are long walkthroughs, up to 128 seconds, talking to camera with titles on screen.
How they write
Own captions are two or three polished sentences, no hashtags, a link to the blog or the bio. Dealer captions carry 8 or 9 hashtags and a consultation call to action.
Who appears
Creators (builtbycarlene, ourhartfulhome, hbwc_woodworks), dealers, designers, an installer. No staff on camera.
Community
The brand leaves its own comment on partner posts but answered no user comments in the posts checked.
modernflamesusa.read: Four own posts in six months, about one every six weeks, and 13 of 17 posts published by partners. All the reach sits there: two Reels by the creator builtbycarlene reached 26,864 and 15,746 views, ourhartfulhome 7,841, while the brand's own Reel got 1,558. With 2,536 followers, the smallest base of the five, the partner Reels reach several times the size of the audience. The brand has outsourced its feed, and so far it works.
borrow: Long creator walkthroughs of a real home. builtbycarlene's two Reels are the most watched content on the account, and one drew 28 comments.
Saying yes to every collab invite from dealers and designers: it fills the grid at no production cost.
Dealers pushing a launch on their own accounts (Landscape Pro Multi).
gaps: Almost no brand voice of its own: one own post every six weeks.
No consistent look: the grid changes style with every partner.

valorfireplaces.headline: The most regular posting schedule, and the lowest reach. A photo feed that funnels to dealers.
points: Visual style
Bright, professional interiors and patios, fireplace as the focal point, neutral palettes, almost no text on image (37 of 48 posts). Product shots for launches and two technical visuals.
Topics and series

Calendar hooks (first day of summer and fall, Canada Day, Labour Day, Halloween), feature explainers (radiant heat, No Power No Problem, HeatShift, HeatSplit, AutoFire, Myth vs Fact), online tools (Design Center, Get a Quote, Find a Dealer) and three launches (HE6 LE, Portrait 530V, G2 insert).
Video style
Only 4 Reels in six months, two own and two from dealers, between 544 and 1,479 views.
How they write
Long, templated captions: a seasonal or benefit hook, two to four sentences of features, then link in bio or find your dealer. 3 to 7 hashtags. Nearly every own post has a call to action.
Who appears
Mostly empty rooms and stock style models. Dealers and installers through shared posts. No creators and no staff on camera.
Community
No replies to comments in the posts checked.
valorfireplaces.read: Valor posts about twice a week, on weekday early afternoons, almost all photos (40 of 48). Engagement is flat: 17 likes and 0.7 comments per post on average, and its best Reel, from a dealer, reached 1,479 views. It is a disciplined, dealer driven catalogue timed to the gas buying season, and nothing changed since mid October. It is the clearest proof that posting more often is not what moves the numbers.
borrow: A call to action on every post that sends people to a dealer or a tool.
Feature explainers that answer a buyer's question (what happens in a power outage, how the heat is distributed).
A steady calendar of seasonal hooks.
gaps: Video is almost absent: 4 Reels in six months.
No people, no creators, no real homes.

napoleonfireplace.headline: The biggest program of the five: a paid council of designers, a home magazine and dealers carry the reach. Own product posts stay small.
points: Visual style

Two tracks. The Design Council template (white marble, the designer's round portrait, a yellow headline, the Napoleon logo, a collage of the project), 30 posts. And polished product in room images, mostly rendered, without text.
Topics and series

The Design Council, about one paid post a week with six designers and builders. Launch waves for every new model (coming soon Reel, launch photo, repeats). House and Home magazine Reels in July and August. Dealer collabs, IDS Vancouver, holidays and themed months.
Video style

36 Reels. Council Reels run 16 to 78 seconds, the designer talking to camera inside the branded frame. Magazine and dealer Reels are home tours or talks. Own product Reels are 14 to 26 second flame and room loops.
How they write
A hook and a flame emoji, the full product name, two to four sentences of benefits or the designer's tip, always 3 hashtags. Link in bio on launch posts and the odd either or question.
Who appears
Paid Design Council designers, a builder, the TV personality Mike Holmes Jr, a DIY creator, House and Home magazine, dealers. No staff except the IDS booth recap.
Community
The brand answered questions on 4 of the 5 posts checked. The only one of the five that does it regularly.
napoleonfireplace.read: Napoleon posts about 3.7 times a week, double anyone else. Its own product Reels get a typical 1,153 views. Its paid Design Council Reels get a typical 10,978 (13 Reels), and the House and Home magazine Reels reached 63,440, 28,617 and 26,067. The NYC dealer that works with us also reached 33,766 for them. 13 of its 17 Council photo posts show 143 to 365 likes against 16 on a typical own photo, which points to paid promotion. The last two, on 22 and 26 October, have 8 and 22 likes, so the promotion may have paused. Reach here is bought and borrowed, and it is consistent.
borrow: A named series with a fixed look, run every week (the Design Council). People recognise it in the feed.
Designers explaining a design idea, with the product as part of the answer.
A home magazine partner: their three House and Home Reels are among the most watched of the five accounts.
gaps: Own product Reels stay around 1,000 views despite the volume.
Much of the reach is paid, so it stops when the budget stops.
The feed is heavy: 97 posts in six months, many of them repeats of the same launch.

dimplex_northamerica.headline: We have the largest audience of the five. Our own Reels reach a small part of it, and the posts that travel are made by partners.
points: Visual style

Warm, staged interiors (most of them look rendered), a beige spec sheet template for launches, and short flame close ups on a dark background for our own Reels. Real homes and real people only appear in partner posts.
Topics and series

Product by product on rotation (Ignite, Optimyst, Revillusion, Vital, Storm Surround), spec sheets for launches, the Canada summer promotion (June and July), the IDS Vancouver run with Caesarstone and Concorde (September), and since September shared Reels with creators and a dealer.
Video style

12 Reels in six months, 8 ours and 4 from partners. Ours run 7 to 48 seconds, flames and product only, with no voice or subtitles except the IDS booth walkthrough. Since October our Reels use trending licensed music.
How we write
A tagline, one or two benefit sentences, a fixed set of 4 or 5 hashtags. Brand voice, no questions to the audience, calls to action only for the promotion or the trade show.
Who appears
Mostly nobody. A rep at the IDS booth, the NYC dealer, and the creators neutralsbydanee, the_rustic_home and this_whole_house.
Community
We answered a question on 1 of the 5 posts checked. On partner posts we leave an emoji comment and the creator does the talking.
dimplex_northamerica.read: From May to early October our feed ran as a catalogue: about 1.3 posts a week, rendered rooms and spec sheets, flat engagement. Our own Reels get a typical 834 views, about 4 for every 100 of our 19,423 followers. The partner Reels are a different scale: the NYC dealer reached 39,165 views, neutralsbydanee 7,534 with 125 comments, this_whole_house 3,587. Since mid October the mix turned to video (all 4 posts after 15 October are Reels), which is the right direction, but our own flame loops still stay under 1,100 views. What our audience responds to is a real person in a real home.
borrow: Partner Reels. Our four best results of the period all came from someone else's account: a dealer and three creators.
The creator collab with neutralsbydanee: 125 comments, against 15 on all our own posts together.
The largest follower base of the five, 19,423, ahead of Napoleon.
The shift to Reels since mid October: all 4 posts after 15 October are Reels.
gaps: Put a person on camera in our own Reels. Flames alone stay under 1,100 views; staff demos at DaVinci reach 38,990 to 65,759.
Turn partner Reels into a monthly plan instead of one off collabs.
Answer every comment, on our posts and on partner posts.
Give every post a next step: find a dealer, see it at a showroom.

_overall.headline: Across five accounts the product on its own does not travel. A person does: a designer, a creator, a dealer, or staff showing something new.
findings: Reels that only show the product and its flames land around the same place everywhere: a typical 834 views for us, 631 for Valor, 1,153 for Napoleon, whatever the size of the account.
Every breakout has a person behind it

The NYC dealer for us (39,165) and for Napoleon (33,766). Napoleon's paid designers (typical 10,978) and House and Home (63,440). A creator for Modern Flames (26,864). DaVinci's staff demoing the holographic fireplace (65,759).
Posting more is not the lever
Napoleon posts 3.7 times a week and Valor 1.8, and Valor has the lowest numbers of all. Modern Flames posts least of its own and its partner Reels reach several times its audience.
We have the audience, not the reach
Dimplex has the most followers, 19,423, and a typical Reel we make ourselves is seen 834 times, about 4 views for every 100 followers.
Napoleon answered questions on 4 of 5 posts checked. We answered on 1 of 5. DaVinci, Modern Flames and Valor did not answer at all.
13 of Napoleon's 17 paid Design Council photos show 143 to 365 likes, against 16 on a typical own photo. Views and comments are the safer way to compare accounts.
plan: Lead with partners. Line up shared Reels with dealers and home creators every month. Our dealer Reel brought 47 times the views of our typical one.
Put a face and a voice in our own Reels: a person demoing what is new (Optimyst RGB, FlexFlame), the way DaVinci does with its holographic fireplace.
Create one named series with a fixed look, the way Napoleon runs its Design Council.
Keep the shift to Reels that started in October, and give each launch three moments: teaser, launch, follow up.
Answer every comment. Only Napoleon does it, and it costs nothing.
